title: 16-06-pace-code-c-2015.pdf — section 123
text:
13. Particular care must be taken when deciding whether to use any
form of approved restraints on a mentally disordered or otherwise
mentally vulnerable person in a locked cell. See paragraph 8.2.
Provisions relating to a person with significant communication
difficulties

14. If a person appears to have significant communication difficulties,
they shall be treated as such for the purposes of this Code in the
absence of advice of a Registered Intermediary to the contrary.
See paragraph 1.7A.

15. A ‘Registered Intermediary’ is a person with specialist
communication skills who has been accredited by the Department
of Justice as a Registered Intermediary to provide assistance to a
detained person who has significant communication difficulties.
See Note 1GG.

16. If the detainee appears to have significant communication
difficulties, the custody officer must, without delay, ensure that a
Registered Intermediary is requested to carry out an assessment of
the detainee. The assessment should take place in the presence of
a responsible third party, such as a solicitor. An officer would not
normally act as the third party, unless the solicitor has consented
to this. Following the assessment, the Registered Intermediary will
advise if he is required to facilitate communication in the
interview. Where a Registered Intermediary is required, he will
 82
advise the interviewing officer of appropriate communication
strategies. See paragraph 3.16.
